findings.title: Embedding response emits only host ids, but the client expects a side-loaded embeddable_hosts collection
findings.body: The serializer declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`, and `Admin::EmbeddingController#show` renders it without `include: [:embeddable_hosts]`. The response therefore contains `embeddable_host_ids` but no root `embeddable_hosts` array. The new client hydration code in store.js looks up each id in `root['embeddable_hosts']`; because that collection is absent, it replaces the ids with an array of `undefined` values. The admin embedding template iterates that array and passes `undefined` into the `embeddable-host` component, so existing allowed hosts do not render and the page can throw when the component reads `host.isNew`. Either include the association in the render call or change the serializer to side-load the host objects.

findings.title: Migration dereferences a result row that may not exist when the old settings were never persisted
findings.body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the `embed_category` join returns at least one row. Site setting defaults are not necessarily stored as rows, and even when `embed_category` exists its value may not match any category name; in either case `execute(...)[0]` is nil and the migration raises before it can finish. The fallback lookup for `uncategorized_category_id` has the same problem. This will abort upgrades on installs that never explicitly changed `embed_category`. Use a nil-safe query result and a valid default/fallback.

findings.title: Old embeddable_hosts values are copied without normalization or escaping
findings.body: The migration interpolates rows from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting directly into an INSERT. The old setting explicitly supported values with `http://`, `https://`, and paths (as shown by the removed specs). Those values are stored verbatim in the new `host` column, but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` only compares `URI(host).host`, so a migrated row like `http://example.com` will never match and existing embeds break. Single quotes in old values also break the generated SQL. Normalize the values through the model/strip scheme and path, downcase the host, and quote/escape them for the INSERT.

findings.title: Allowed-host lookup is case-sensitive for the incoming URL
findings.body: The query is `where('lower(host) = ?', host)`, but the bound `host` comes directly from `URI(host).host` without being downcased. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer or embed URL with an uppercase host (for example `HTTP://EVILTROUT.COM/...`) will not match a stored lowercase host even though it should be allowed. Downcase the input or compare `lower(host) = lower(?)`.

findings.title: Missing host crashes before_validation instead of producing a validation error
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil, which can happen when an API client omits the parameter or creates an `EmbeddableHost` without a host. Because this runs in `before_validation`, the record never reaches the format validator and the controller returns a 500 instead of a 422 with validation errors. Guard against nil (or use `to_s`) before stripping.

findings.title: Hosts are not unique, so the category for a host can be ambiguous
findings.body: The model only validates host format, and the new table has no unique index or uniqueness validation on `host`. An admin can create two rows for the same host with different categories, and `record_for_host` will return whichever row the database returns first. Imported topics then land in an arbitrary category. Add a uniqueness constraint on the normalized host (for example a unique index on `lower(host)`) and validate it in the model.

findings.title: Missing record in update/destroy causes an unhandled 500
findings.body: Both `update` and `destroy` fetch with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call methods on the result. If the id is invalid or the host was deleted, `host` is nil; `save_host(nil)` or `nil.destroy` raises and returns a 500. Use `find_by` and render a proper not-found response when the record is absent.

findings.title: New admin CRUD controller is only tested for class inheritance
findings.body: The only test asserts that `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` subclasses `Admin::AdminController`. There are no request specs covering create/update/destroy, invalid/missing host values, category fallback, or non-admin access. This leaves the new admin API unprotected against regressions such as nil-host 500s, missing-record 500s, and incorrect category assignment. Add controller specs that exercise the actions and authorization.
